newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stock exchange says to press stamp duty cut.
newsitem.headline: HK stock exchange says to press stamp duty cut.

text.p: Hong Kong's Stock Exchange said on Wednesday after Financial Secretary Donald Tsang announced his 1997/98 budget it would continue to discuss with the government to lower stamp duty on stock transactions.

"It still holds the view that stamp duty should not be linked with brokerage commission as the former is solely a revenue raising measure and the latter a service fee," the Stock Exchange said in a statement.

"It is important to note that Hong Kong has the lowest brokerage commission amongst major markets but our stamp duty is the hignest compared with markets like London, Tokyo and other markets in the region," the exchange said.
Tsang did not make any changes to stamp duty, which still remained at 0.3 percent on each stock transition.
